mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 4% in the month prior to the decision is associated with a near-term negative S&P 500 20-day forward return due to higher discounting of future cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4% in the prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero when FEDFUNDS > 4% in prior month (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in consumer pay growth (HOUST) predict negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns as labor market weakness dampens corporate earnings expectations.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while HOUST decreases in the same month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns remain positive despite the combined signal (p-value > 0.05 in a two-tailed test).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly surge in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 2% above the prior month's level coincides with a positive S&P 20-day forward return as it signals robust economic momentum supporting equity valuations.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative when INDPRO grows >2% (p-value < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained double-dip in inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 2% for two consecutive months triggers a negative S&P 60-day forward return as markets anticipate higher policy rates and lower equity valuations.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p-value > 0.05) during the inflationary period.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% in the prior month, without a corresponding rise in inflation (CPIAUCSL), predicts a positive S&P 5-day forward return as markets anticipate rate cuts.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 4% while CPIAUCSL remains flat or declining in the prior month
regime_hint: labor market tightening with stable prices
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not positive when UNRATE < 4% and CPIAUCSL does not decline (p-value > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly PAYEMS increase exceeding 50,000 when INDPRO is flat predicts a negative S&P 20-day forward return as excess labor may signal softening demand.
Note: Since only available proxies are PAYEMS, INDPRO, etc., the following uses PAYEMS as labor proxy. Adjusted to fit constraints.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 50,000 and INDPRO unchanged in the same month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not negative when the signal occurs (p-value > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS below 1% for three consecutive months predicts a positive S&P 60-day forward return as markets anticipate rate cuts and increased liquidity.
candidate_trigger: 3-month FEDFUNDS MA falls below 1% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during the period (p-value > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) of at least 3% predicts a negative S&P 20-day forward return as it suggests weakening manufacturing demand and tighter supply conditions.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases for three consecutive months by at least 3%
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not negative when INDPRO declines as specified (p-value > 0.05).
